solutions.check: 30 of 32 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Machine not designed right in legend

indicators.note: the shuffled letters plus R are placed inside the word for legend

parts.note: a legend is the caption printed under a picture

indicators.note: something designed has been worked out into a new shape, so the letters of the little word beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some machine was badly made, and the right-hand part is set into a legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not designed' reads as 'unplanned', but the first word is fodder: its rearrangement and R go into the legend, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrivance or gadget, especially an odd improvised one, is a machine in the loose everyday sense.

clue.text: Sound coming from dovecote, well I never!

definitions.meaning: the soft murmuring noise pigeons make
a British exclamation of surprise, like 'blimey'

explanation.definitionFit: The noise of doves is so named, and the same syllable is a mild British cry of astonishment.

clue.text: Chip, neat, almost catching hole, others teeing off?

indicators.note: to tee off is to start a round of golf, so each of the other words gives up its starting letter

explanation.surface: A golfer's chip almost drops into the hole while the rest of the group are still at the first tee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' is both the last word read and the instruction's subject: the initials of every word but 'Chip' spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla chip of the Mexican snack kind, usually served topped with melted cheese.

clue.text: Sally having job corking wine? Sling away!

indicators.note: a cork is pushed into a bottle, so the job goes inside what is left of the wine
away tells us to remove the word Sling from the wine's name

parts.note: Riesling is a white grape wine
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A girl called Sally gets a job stopping wine bottles, and is told to throw away her sling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sling away!' reads like a cheerful 'fire away', but it is an instruction to drop those letters from the grape's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty comeback, as is a sharp retort.

clue.text: Criticize a religious leader a degree less for informal headgear

parts.note: to pan a play is to slate it

indicators.note: less means the degree's letters are taken away from the holy man's title

parts.note: Mahatma, 'great soul', is the title of a revered Indian holy man such as Gandhi
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a religious leader, docking a qualification, over his casual hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes the MA at the end of MAHATMA, leaving MAHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The light straw hat from Ecuador is casual summer wear rather than formal dress.

clue.text: Poem's considerable length doubled, though introduction missed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a tidy sum is a considerable one

indicators.note: the abbreviation is written twice

explanation.surface: A poem of great length gets twice as long but loses its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction missed' drops the T of TIDY to leave IDY; 'doubled' gives LL. The 's is 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pastoral piece of verse describing a peaceful rural scene is this kind of poem.

clue.text: Country not entirely upsetting perfect queen

indicators.note: not entirely means one end letter of the turned-over run is left off
in a down clue upsetting turns the letters upside down, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as the letters A and I
Regina is Latin for queen, as in a monarch's signature

explanation.surface: A nation is described as not quite overthrowing an ideal queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns AI + REGINA over to give ANIGERIA; 'not entirely' then drops its first letter. A1 (first-rate) is written AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African republic is a country, the most populous on that continent.

clue.text: Quiet without silence, initially what?

indicators.note: without means the letter is left out

parts.note: hush means quiet

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is the one removed

explanation.surface: Someone asks for quiet, and then, puzzled, wonders what has happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes the S (from 'silence initially') out of HUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: This grunt is an informal way of asking someone to repeat or explain, much like 'eh?'.

clue.text: Unskilled worker receiving benefit at home secured by the bank

indicators.note: the worker's word takes in the next word's letters

parts.note: a hobo was originally an itinerant labourer in the US, doing casual unskilled work
use means benefit or advantage, as in 'of no use'

explanation.surface: A labourer on benefits is at home but his house has been repossessed by the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank is not a lender but a riverbank: this home is moored to it. A hobo was a migrant labourer in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat fitted out as a dwelling and tied up at the riverside is a home held by the bank.

clue.text: Dwarf a normal size? That's a satisfactory compromise

parts.note: Happy is one of the Seven Dwarfs in the Snow White story
medium is the middle clothing size between small and large

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dwarf is normal-sized, and calls that a fair middle ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a sensible middle course between two extremes, an acceptable compromise.

clue.text: Publishers retain small volume, an extremely classy possession

indicators.note: the publishers' letters hold the small volume inside them

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press
cc, cubic centimetres, is a small measure of volume
taken as written

indicators.note: the outermost letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: A publishing house keeps a little book, a very classy thing to own.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'small volume' is not a book but cubic centimetres; OUP is Oxford University Press.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupancy means holding or occupying a place, which is a form of possession.

clue.text: Start to giggle behind surly type

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the rump is one's behind, the backside

explanation.surface: Someone starts to giggle behind a bad-tempered person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position but is a noun, the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumpy, bad-tempered person is called by this informal name.

clue.text: After work, huge number viewing marsupial

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
OS, outsize, is the clothing label for very large
a sum is a number, the total of an addition

explanation.surface: After work, a great many people go to look at a marsupial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huge number' is not one idea but two: OS (outsize) and SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The American tree-dwelling pouched mammal is the only marsupial native north of Mexico.

clue.text: Time spent working for us, chief gathered, under nought!

indicators.note: in a down clue the rearranged letters sit below the zero

parts.note: nought is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: gathered together into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The boss calls a meeting to complain that our hours are worth nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' rearranges FOR US CHIEF; 'under' places that below O.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours in the day during which business is done or a professional sees clients are working time.

clue.text: Criminal nearly getting caught in crime

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
criminal suggests something bent or corrupt, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A criminal very nearly gets caught in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges NEARLY into LARENY, with C put in by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft of personal property is a crime with this legal name.

clue.text: Cover up sweet

definitions.meaning: to avoid or blur an issue deliberately, to paper over it
a soft confection made from sugar, butter and milk

explanation.definitionFit: To evade the truth is to blur it, and the same word is a soft sugary confection.

clue.text: Ridiculously smart idea, to prepare for the stage

indicators.note: ridiculously points to letters arranged absurdly, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ridiculous but clever idea for putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt a story as a play is to make it ready for performance on stage.

clue.text: Bridle at journalist's love for Italian

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often a jobbing one
amore is the Italian word for love

explanation.surface: Someone bridles at a reporter's affection for an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridle' looks like a verb, 'take offence at', but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitless bridle working on a horse's nose is known by this Western riding name.

clue.text: Eruption as black relative is run over by vehicle

indicators.note: in a down entry, being run over puts the vehicle on top

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: A black relative is run over by a car, a dreadful event.
explanation.definitionFit: A boil-like eruption on the skin, a large painful swelling, has this medical name.

clue.text: Sign card

definitions.meaning: a letter or symbol used in writing
an eccentric or amusing person, as in 'he's a real card'

explanation.definitionFit: A written symbol is so called, and so is an odd, colourful person, a card.

clue.text: Supporter demanding a pass, yet converted

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan demands a free pass yet has become a convert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges YET into YTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant in church ritual, or more widely a devoted follower, is a supporter.

clue.text: The King and I, after a little time, finding musical direction

indicators.note: the I comes after the T

parts.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun, the boy king of Egypt
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: After a short while, people discover a musical, The King and I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' is the famous musical, but here the king is Tutankhamun.
explanation.definitionFit: An instruction in a score meaning all players or singers together is a musical direction.

clue.text: Capital — could it be keeping party on the rise?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards
the question holds the party within it

parts.note: is it? asks whether it could be so
Lib is short for Liberal, a political party

explanation.surface: A capital city asks whether it is keeping a party in power on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts LIB in IS IT (ISILIBT); 'on the rise' turns that over to give the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Georgia, in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Take everything in, as man takes a beating

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A man is badly beaten and must take it all in.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen to someone fully without interrupting is to take in all they say.

clue.text: One's an idiot before weight lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the pieces turns them to read upwards

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: An idiot drops his weights before lifting them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns PREWT upside down; 'One's an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly or annoying person, a nitwit, is called by this informal name.

clue.text: Oxbridge application, perhaps, consistent

parts.note: Oxford and Cambridge are examples of a uni, a university
an application form is the paper you fill in

explanation.surface: A form applying to Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Oxbridge as just an example of a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Unvarying, alike in every case, as a consistent standard is.

clue.text: Modern style beginning to offend constituent

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a constituent is a part of something

explanation.surface: A modern style has a component which begins to offend.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s abstract art movement using optical illusions.

clue.text: One can start to unwind about halfway through honeymoon

indicators.note: about turns the can and the starting letter round together

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word
the letter at the exact middle of the nine-letter word

explanation.surface: One can start to relax halfway through a honeymoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TIN plus U backwards to give UNIT; Y is the fifth of the nine letters of 'honeymoon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity is oneness, and the number one is called unity in mathematics.

clue.text: English nation cut zero sandwiches, providing Mexican food

indicators.note: the zero word wraps round the shortened nation

parts.note: nada is Spanish for nothing

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Chile is a South American nation

explanation.surface: An English country cuts its sandwiches to nothing but provides Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of the South American nation, and 'sandwiches' wraps the Spanish word for nothing around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla rolled round a filling and covered in chilli sauce is a Mexican dish.

clue.text: Line taken in the middle of the month?

indicators.note: only the middle letters of the word are used

parts.note: March is a month

explanation.surface: A line is drawn in the middle of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: The month is March; its middle gives the curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved line, part of a circle's circumference, is an arc.

clue.text: Date found in suitcase, eaten

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A date fruit is found in a suitcase, half eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The date is not the fruit but a romantic outing: to see someone is to date them.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out with someone romantically is to be seeing them.

clue.text: Margin in cup tie is possibly less embarrassing

indicators.note: the edging goes inside the rearranged letters
possibly shows the letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: a hem is an edge or margin of cloth

explanation.surface: A cup tie's margin of victory might be less of an embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CUP TIE IS to EUPISTIC, with HEM inside by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism replaces a blunt word with a milder one, so the wording is less embarrassing.
